blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights a critical issue in VM benchmarking: many studies assume benchmarks reach a steady state of peak performance after a few iterations, but Barrett et al.'s paper reveals this assumption is often false. The authors conduct an exhaustive, three-year study across multiple languages (Java, JavaScript, Python, Lua, PHP, Ruby) and VMs, using controlled experiments to analyze warmup behavior. They employ changepoint analysis to detect when (or if) a VM reaches a steady state and whether that state represents peak performance. The results are alarming: only 37% of (VM, benchmark) pairs show consistent 'good' warmup behavior (flat or classic warmup), while nearly half exhibit 'bad inconsistent' behavior (slowdown or no steady state). This unpredictability undermines the reliability of VM optimizations based on microbenchmarks, as ineffective or harmful optimizations may be incorrectly adopted.
